# Run a customer demonstration and evaluation

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When a qualified prospect needs evidence that the product can meet an agreed use case. A customer-reviewed pilot result and explicit purchase, further-test or stop decision.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Agree the use case and success criteria

human · human approval required


Confirm the customer sponsor, users, problem, scope and observable success measures. Identify what the demonstration cannot prove and which requested capabilities are unavailable.

- Sources: [GitLab customer onboarding](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/segment/cse/customer-onboarding/)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Approve pilot terms and data access

human · human approval required


Review the environment, data rights, security, costs, support and exit arrangements with the authorized owners. Keep production integrations and sensitive customer data out until their required approvals are complete.

- Sources: [GitLab customer onboarding](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/segment/cse/customer-onboarding/)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Provision the approved test configuration

manual form/portal · human approval required · hard to undo


Use the authorized account and data to configure the agreed scope. Verify participant access, logging and rollback, and record the product version and setup dependencies.

- Sources: [GitLab customer onboarding](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/segment/cse/customer-onboarding/)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Collect reproducible pilot evidence

agent-runnable


Track task outcomes, adoption, defects, support effort and customer feedback against the agreed criteria. Record limitations and avoid substituting a curated demonstration for representative operating results.

- Sources: [GitLab customer onboarding](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/segment/cse/customer-onboarding/)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Review the outcome with the customer

human · human approval required


Discuss the evidence, unresolved blockers and required commercial or technical next steps. Authorize any extension separately and remove or migrate pilot data and access according to the agreed terms.

- Verify: A customer-reviewed pilot result and explicit purchase, further-test or stop decision.
- Sources: [GitLab customer onboarding](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/segment/cse/customer-onboarding/)
